argument: Any finite set of $n$ points in high-dimensional Euclidean space can be embedded into $O(\!\left(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n\right))$ dimensions while preserving all pairwise distances within multiplicative distortion $1\pm\varepsilon$. Random projections often realize the guarantee.
boundary: The guarantee concerns finite Euclidean point sets and pairwise distances.
Very small distortion or structured non-Euclidean geometry may require more dimensions.
Projection can destroy interpretability and task-relevant coordinates.
claim: Any finite set of $n$ points in high-dimensional Euclidean space can be embedded into $O(\!\left(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n\right))$ dimensions while preserving all pairwise distances within multiplicative distortion $1\pm\varepsilon$. Random projections often realize the guarantee.
interpretation: Use this theorem as a precise compression root, not as permission to assume that arbitrary semantic information survives dimensionality reduction.

argument: For every covariate stratum relevant to the target population, each compared treatment must have nonzero probability. Without overlap, observed data contain no counterfactual comparison for unsupported regions, and estimates rely on extrapolation.
boundary: Near-violations can cause extreme weights and unstable estimates even when probabilities are technically nonzero.
Structural positivity violations may require redefining the target population or intervention.
High-dimensional covariates make overlap difficult to assess.
claim: For every covariate stratum relevant to the target population, each compared treatment must have nonzero probability. Without overlap, observed data contain no counterfactual comparison for unsupported regions, and estimates rely on extrapolation.
interpretation: A new Principle should state its empirical support region. Universal treatment claims based on one narrow operating regime violate this root.
